# Database schema changes in this repository

This repository's database schema is managed with SQL Server Data Tools (SSDT). A change is
authored as an edit to a table definition, built into a dacpac, and deployed through Azure
DevOps into Octopus. The deployment always runs with the data-loss guard on, and it cannot be
relaxed for a single deploy.

A workflow named ssdt-agent guides these changes. Its full content is vendored in this
repository under `ssdt-agent/` — the operation skills, the agent roles, the record standard,
and worked examples. Use it whenever you help with a schema or data change.

## When to use it

- A request to change the data model — "make Email required", "add a reference to Customer",
  "rename this attribute", "drop that table", "turn this text column into a lookup" — is an
  authoring task. Take the intake role first, then the change-author role. If this editor offers
  custom agents they are named `intake` and `change-author`; otherwise read
  `ssdt-agent/agents/intake.md` and `ssdt-agent/agents/change-author.md` and follow them.
- A request to review a schema pull request is a review task. Take the `reviewer` role, or read
  `ssdt-agent/agents/reviewer.md`.
- In an editor with neither custom agents nor skills (Visual Studio 2022), the prompt files
  under `.github/prompts/` are the entry: `#prompt:ssdt-schema-change` runs the whole
  authoring flow (intake then change-author) in one conversation; `#prompt:ssdt-intake`,
  `#prompt:ssdt-change-author`, `#prompt:ssdt-review` adopt one role at a time.

## The one rule that governs all of it

You cannot tell how a schema change will behave by reading its SQL. The same edit ships one way
against an empty table and another way against a table that holds rows. So do not classify a
change from the text. Publish it to a disposable copy of the database and read what the
deployment engine does — that result is the classification. Each operation skill under
`ssdt-agent/skills/op/` says how to prove its own change.

If proving cannot run — no local database, the build fails, the tool is missing — stop and tell
the developer. Do not fall back on a guess from the SQL text. A guess is the exact failure this
workflow exists to prevent.

## Loading a skill

On a schema-change request, open `ssdt-agent/skills/INDEX.md` — one line per skill, its
trigger phrases written in the developer's own words. Pick the matching row, read that skill
file, then the shared-knowledge files it points to under `ssdt-agent/skills/_index/`. Follow
the skill; do not re-derive its reasoning. (If your editor auto-activates a skill, its file
routes you to the same in-tree body — follow it.)

## Writing the pull request and the review

Every record you write — the pull request body, a review comment, a disposition — follows the
register in `ssdt-agent/THE_RECORD.md`: state the finding, put its evidence beneath, name the
next step, and admit what was not checked. Teach the developer in conversation, never in the
record.

## Two boundaries

- Publish only to a disposable copy of the database. Never point a publish profile at a real
  environment.
- The environments on this estate are named Dev, QA, UAT, and Prod. There is no environment
  called "Test".
